items.title: Isaiah Morgan Interview, 1958-12-01
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...who the best trumpet players were in the carnet, on the carnet in this city. Do you remember Oliver or Kepard or anybody like that? ... INTERVIEWEE: I remember Juaro, Manuel Perez... Joe Oliver and Manuel Perez. Now Freddie Carford, I heard him a couple of times but I don't know...

ctx.x: Well, his daddy was playing bass violin and old Tom Albin on Begundry and St. Peter. Tom used to be his trumpet player. And they always wanted to carry me over there. And they carried me to Passpegoula. That's the first time I had a chance to get over there. And after I got over there once, then this, the fellow was running the pressing shop. He seen me. And Tom and them couldn't come and asked me could I get a band. I told him yeah. And we was, I said, young Sam Morgan band. And we went over there and from that…
I wondered in 1915 when you moved up here, who the best trumpet players were in the carnet, on the carnet in this city. Do you remember Oliver or Kepard or anybody like that?

I remember Juaro, Manuel Perez. I used to like to hear them men play trumpet because it takes three trumpet players to play them fumes and parades. And them too used to play the parade, you see. And both of them was loud and they could play. You see them. Joe Oliver and Manuel Perez. Now Freddie Carford, I heard him a couple of times but I don't know, he just got on out of my sight. I didn't, I never was around no place where he was playing regular. He went on away.
